thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 PG: node-status-change - infer-pool-usw-03 moved to NotReady (kubelet restart detected) x3 within 180s. Affected pods: 28, impacted routes: inference-usw-*, error class: kubelet-flip. Paging oncall: @Tilly
Tilly (oncall): ack. jumping in. any customer-facing errors?
Sam (eng): yep, spikes of 502/504 from the west region; our request router shows backend disconnects to infer-pool-usw-03 and a couple others. Low-level OOMs on some containers before the kubelet restart.
Maya (eng-runtime): noted. I’m pulling logs for the runtime on that node now. can someone cordon it so we stop scheduling new inferences?
Cheng (infra): cordoning infer-pool-usw-03 now: `kubectl cordon infer-pool-usw-03`
Priya (support): customers reported timeouts in the EU/US west zones. Support is drafting a brief to send to affected accounts.
Tilly (oncall): good. Sam/Cheng — any immediate mitigation besides cordon? auto-scale?
Sam (eng): scaling up warm nodes in the pool by +2 as a short-term buffer. `kubectl scale deployment/infer-pool --replicas=18 -n inference` (starting now).
Maya (eng-runtime): pulling kubelet/journal logs: `journalctl -u kubelet -o short-iso --since "10 minutes ago" | tail -n 200` shows repeated `OOMKilled` of container runtime (nvidia-driver-manager) around the same time, then kubelet restarted. grabbing dmesg and container logs.
Maya (eng-runtime): snippet:
```
May 01 14:03:21 infer-pool-usw-03 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 27481 (nvidia-ferm) score 1234 or sacrifice child
May 01 14:03:22 infer-pool-usw-03 kubelet[1234]: Node not ready: Kubelet stopped; restarting
```
Sam (eng): that looks like GPU driver process OOM -> kubelet restart -> node NotReady. Could be runaway memory use in one of the inference containers (large batch + quantize) or kernel driver leak.
Cheng (infra): I’m spinning an identical node from the same image to isolate if it’s infra image related. Also fetching `nvidia-smi -q` output from other nodes.
Priya (support): ETA for customer note? we should confirm if any SLAs hit.
Tilly (oncall): hold off public note until we confirm scope. Priya, draft an internal summary now; external every 30 mins unless major outage.
Maya (eng-runtime): setting temporary routing policy: divert traffic away from west for heavy batch requests and favor eu-east for now. Updating routing rules in the gateway: `route update infer-route --prefer-region eu-east --max-burst 100`
Sam (eng): also enabling fallback to smaller model variant (gpt-medium-quant) for routes hitting the west to reduce memory pressure: pushing config change to router.
Cheng (infra): spun a replacement node `infer-pool-usw-07` and joined to cluster. No immediate crash on join. I’ll keep it drained until we confirm image/drivers.
Maya (eng-runtime): collecting kubelet logs + container logs for the OOM'd pod. attaching a small repro to run heavy batch locally to try replicate.
Sam (eng): if this is a model-side memory blowup, we should revert the last rollout from yesterday that changed batch sizing. Anyone see a canary change?
Tilly (oncall): rollout history shows a config update at 03:42 (batch-size hint) by @sam. Can we rollback that change?
Sam (eng): Rolling back now to the previous config: `kubectl apply -f infer-config-v1.yaml` -> `rolled config back`
Maya (eng-runtime): after rollback, I'm not seeing new OOMs in the logs for the test container. telemetry for batch latency looks stable in the test env. good sign.
Cheng (infra): re-enabling one drained node to service: `kubectl uncordon infer-pool-usw-03` but keeping pod eviction disabled until kubelet stable.
incident-bot: NOTE: pager duty escalation in 12m if no resolution.
Priya (support): sending internal note to AE/customer success + flagged top 10 accounts for follow-up.
Tilly (oncall): summarize current state: 1) cause: suspected batch-size config bump causing runtime OOM -> gpu driver process OOM -> kubelet restart -> NotReady flaps. 2) Mitigations: rollback config, cordon/uncordon/replace nodes, scale up warm nodes, route heavy traffic away and enable smaller model variant. 3) Impact: intermittent 5xx/timeouts in us-west for ~15-40m for a subset of customers. 4) Next steps: deeper postmortem (Maya/Sam/Cheng).
Maya (eng-runtime): I’ll follow up with crash dumps and kernel logs, and add evts to the incident timeline.
Sam (eng): I’ll create a quick PR to add guard rails: reject batch sizes > X for that model and automated rollback if node OOM signals detected.
Cheng (infra): I’ll check driver versions across fleet and open a ticket with cloud provider if we find a kernel-driver mismatch.
Tilly (oncall): thanks team. mark this thread with :white_check_mark: when you’ve added your follow-ups. I’m going to update the incident channel and set a 1hr follow-up meeting.
Sam (eng): ✅ updated PR and ticket links: https://goto/repo/pr/1234 , https://goto/infra/ticket/987
Maya (eng-runtime): ✅ uploaded logs to S3 and added notes to the incident doc.
Priya (support): ✅ internal note sent to customers flagged; will send external comms if ETA extends.
Tilly (oncall): closing the active page for now — continue monitoring.
